title: FinFET Inspection - Pits Detection on Teron SL650
subtitle: Post-Deposition Quality Validation for 14nm Node Manufacturing
author: Maria Gonzalez

sections.1_OBJECTIVE:
This test case validates the capability of the Teron SL650 system to detect and classify Pits defects during post-deposition inspection at the 14nm technology node. The test is conducted at Milpitas Fab B to ensure manufacturing quality standards are met for 300mm wafer production.

The primary objective is to verify that the inspection system meets the required detection sensitivity and classification accuracy for Pits defects that are critical to yield at the 14nm node. This test case is part of the ongoing qualification program for the Teron SL650 platform.
sections.2_SCOPE:
- Product Line: Teron SL650
- Inspection Type: FinFET Inspection
- Target Defect: Pits
- Process Step: Post-Deposition
- Wafer Size: 300mm
- Technology Node: 14nm
- Fab Location: Milpitas Fab B

This test case applies to all Teron SL650 systems deployed at Milpitas Fab B for post-deposition monitoring in the 14nm manufacturing line. Results from this test are used to establish baseline performance metrics and to qualify new recipe configurations.
sections.3_TEST_CONFIGURATION:
System: Teron SL650
Software Version: v11.2.500
Recipe: FINFET_INSPECTION_14nm_POST_DEPOSITION
Illumination Mode: Brightfield
Scan Speed: Medium (149 mm/s)
Pixel Size: 0.25μm
Edge Exclusion: 5mm
Sampling Plan: 21-point sampling
sections.4_TEST_PROCEDURE:
1. Power on the Teron SL650 system and allow 30-minute warm-up period.
2. Load the calibration wafer and run the standard calibration routine.
3. Verify calibration results are within specification (±2% tolerance).
4. Load the test wafer onto the stage using the automated handler.
5. Select the 'FinFET Inspection' recipe from the recipe library.
6. Configure detection sensitivity to target Pits defects.
7. Set scan parameters: full wafer scan with edge exclusion of 3mm.
8. Initiate the inspection run and monitor real-time defect map.
9. Upon completion, review the defect density map and classification results.
10. Export results to the factory automation system (SECS/GEM interface).
11. Compare results against the golden reference baseline.
12. Document any anomalies and generate the summary report.
sections.5_ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- Defect detection sensitivity must meet 14nm node requirements
- False positive rate shall not exceed 5% of total detected events
- Scan throughput must be ≥ 106 wafers per hour
- Classification accuracy shall be ≥ 95% for known defect types
- Repeatability (3-sigma) shall be within ±1.0% for FinFET Inspection
- System uptime during test shall be ≥ 98%
- All results must be traceable through the MES integration
- Measurement correlation with reference tool shall be ≥ 0.94 R²
sections.6_TEST_RESULTS:
Test Execution Date: 2024-04-26
Wafers Tested: 44
Total Defects Found: 1270
Defect Density: 179.67 defects/cm²
Nuisance Rate: 3.1%
Capture Rate: 90.0%
Test Duration: 442 minutes
System Uptime: 96.6%

Result Classification: CONDITIONAL PASS
sections.7_OBSERVATIONS:
a) The Teron SL650 demonstrated acceptable performance in detecting Pits at the 14nm node.

b) The capture rate requires optimization of the detection algorithm.

c) Nuisance rate is within acceptable limits.

d) Throughput metrics met production requirements without sensitivity compromise.

e) The defect review station correlation was within specification.
sections.8_CORRECTIVE_ACTIONS:
The following corrective actions are recommended:

1. Review edge-zone detection parameters for optimization.
2. Schedule follow-up test after recipe optimization.
3. Monitor performance over next 30 production days.
